therapeutic_hypothesis.proposed_mechanism: PD-L1 immune checkpoint blockade and CTLA-4 immune checkpoint blockade
therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: T-cell activation and anti-tumor immune response
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: Patients with locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer, stratified by PD-L1 expression

results.effect_size: OS HR 0.63 (95% CI: 0.42-0.93) for Sub-study A; OS HR 0.80 (95% CI: 0.61-1.05, p=0.109) for Sub-study B; PFS HR 0.71 (95% CI: 0.49-1.04) for Sub-study A; PFS HR 0.77 (95% CI: 0.59-1.01, p=0.056) for Sub-study B
subgroup_findings: Sub-study A (PD-L1 selected): Durvalumab showed OS benefit vs SoC (11.7 vs 6.8 months)
Sub-study B (unselected): No significant OS benefit for combination vs SoC (11.5 vs 8.7 months, p=0.109)
ORR higher in Sub-study A durvalumab vs SoC (35.5% vs 12.5%)
Combination did not improve outcomes vs durvalumab monotherapy
safety_signals: Febrile neutropenia in standard of care arm
Cardiac events including myocardial infarction, cardiac failure, cardiac arrest
Hematologic toxicities including anemia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia
results.dose_information: Durvalumab by IV infusion, Tremelimumab by IV infusion, specific doses not provided in results

context.comparator: Standard of care (vinorelbine, gemcitabine, or erlotinib)
